A1.justification: Both PDFs describe NarrativeBridge, its CTN caption benchmark, and the CEN architecture. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite reorganized sections and displays.

before.justification: v2 reports original captioning experiments, architecture ablations, cross-dataset evaluations, human ratings, and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds encoder controls, prompt ablations, caption-quality statistics, and LLM-based evaluations.

M1.justification: The caption-generation prompt, EMScore filtering threshold, two-stage CEN architecture, separate cause/effect encoders, feature concatenation, and training losses remain unchanged. New experimental variants are ablations, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MSVD- and MSR-VTT-derived CTN captioning tasks and retain the unlabeled-video demonstration. The more explicit MSVD-CTN and MSRVTT-CTN names clarify existing coverage; the new LLM evaluations assess the same captioning outputs.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds single-CLIP and two-CLIP controls without Stage 1 fine-tuning. Existing external comparators remain unchanged. EJointCE becomes Ecombined, and the cross-dataset variants receive new names without changing their comparator identities.

E3.justification: Appendix A.9 introduces Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct judging of binary temporal-order and causal-chain correctness across the combined datasets. New experiments remove prompt requirements or Stage 1 fine-tuning. Section 3.1 also changes the human-sampling description to proportional stratification, although Appendix A.5 retains 50 samples per dataset; this establishes a reporting change, not a verified rerun.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands validation with two encoder fine-tuning controls, six individual prompt-requirement ablations in Appendix A.2, an initial-caption EMScore distribution, and LLM-based assessment of architecture ablations in Appendix A.9. These examine component necessity, prompt failure modes, and filtering effectiveness beyond v2's retained analyses.

E5.justification: v3 newly reports an 8.2% sampling margin of error at 90% confidence. The human-rating standard deviations, ICC of 0.87, and its 95% confidence interval remain unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark, human-rating, and matched ablation scores are unchanged, but substantial additional results appear. Table 2 adds frozen single/two-CLIP CIDEr scores of 46.23/53.84 on MSVD-CTN. Table 6 reports temporal/causal scores of 81.2%/84.5% for CEN versus 52.1%/48.3% for GIT. v3 also adds LLM ablation scores, prompt-failure examples, and caption statistics, including 66.4% initially exceeding EMScore 0.2.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–9 are retained. Added pooling explanations and empirical judging criteria introduce no new theorem, proof, derivation, or substantive formal assumption.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a novel CTN benchmark, a dedicated CEN architecture, superior causal-temporal captioning, and cross-dataset generalization. Condensed wording and clearer dataset labels preserve these contributions and their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations connecting omitted prompt requirements to specific failure modes and encoder fine-tuning to improved caption understanding. It emphasizes competitiveness of retained zero-shot results and shortens the limitations discussion, removing the explicit assumption of causal and temporal coherence while retaining complex-causality and spatial-reasoning limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix A.9 identifies the new evaluator model, inputs, and binary scoring tasks, but supplies no exact judging prompt. A new reproducibility statement promises CEN weights alongside the previously promised captions. Appendix A.1's implementation settings are unchanged; the explicit PyTorch disclosure is removed.

R1.justification: v3 adds Awan et al. (2024), Attend-Fusion, and Ventura et al. (2024), Learning Text-to-Video Retrieval from Image Captioning. These support existing discussions without substantially changing the positioning against captioning and causal-reasoning research.

P1.justification: v3 condenses introductory and related-work prose, standardizes CTN dataset terminology, moves dataset descriptions into results, and places ablations before qualitative results. Ethics and reproducibility statements are added, while the overall narrative and most appendix text remain intact.

P2.justification: Result presentation expands substantially: Table 1 becomes full-width, Table 2 moves and gains rows, and v3 adds an EMScore histogram, two LLM-evaluation tables, and six prompt-ablation result figures with corresponding prompt boxes. Existing illustrations are relocated or renumbered, and video-game frames are partially masked in Figures 6 and 17.

improvement.justification: The new encoder controls and prompt ablations better test design choices, while Appendix A.9 supplements generic caption scores with targeted temporal and causal evaluation. These additions strengthen support for the retained claims. The gain is limited by incomplete LLM-judge documentation and validation, and by the conflicting human-sampling descriptions in Section 3.1 and Appendix A.5.
